I have played a handful of games using their systems that spanned several years.

My first venture was Spycraft 2.0. It was a fun system with entertaining archetypes. The customizations and toys characters could get was highly entertaining. Unfortunately there was only one campaign in Spycraft, but it was still fun.

I was in probably half a dozen campaigns spanning several years using their Fantasy Craft line. They don't have a bazillion expansion books like D&D has, so you have about a dozen classes to choose from. However what they lack in quantity they make up for in quality. Each class, while filling an archetype, can be tweaked to feel quite different. Take their Soldier as an example. This one lines up with D&D's Fighter, but it never has a dead level, and you have enough skill points and options to become a monster on the battle field (with fun feats to choose from based on weapon/armor preference), a silver tongued merchant, a competent blacksmith, or some combination there of. On the GM side there is some learning curve, but once you get it it's easy. One of the biggest advantages I know of is their NPC creation system. It's point based as opposed to mixing and matching classes, so once you have a grasp on it a NPC can be thrown together and fully statted out in minutes from a simple concept.

Mistborn is their third, and in practice only, setting. They acquired the rights to produce it, and based on the resources they're pouring into it it's apparently doing quite well. I don't have any experience with it outside of reading the first book. Does anyone here have any hands on experience with this setting?
Anyone have any experience with Crafty Games?
